chapter_title: The Oracle and the Algorithm, Part 2: The Algorithm
learning_objective: The learner will infer how changing the temperature changes which next word a language model chooses and how often, answering at least 4 of 5 prediction questions correctly before the sampled results are revealed.
specification:
Type: microsim **sim-id:** next-word-temperature-toy
**Library:** p5.js
**Status:** Specified
**Bloom Level:** Understand
**Bloom Verb:** infer
**Learning Objective:** The learner will infer how changing the temperature changes which next word a language model chooses and how often, answering at least 4 of 5 prediction questions correctly before the sampled results are revealed. **Prerequisites:** large language model, token, next-word prediction, temperature, probability (defined in "Large Language Model" and "Next-Word Prediction" above). **Evidence of Mastery:** For each of five challenge questions, the learner commits to one answer before pressing Reveal. An answer is correct when it matches the Correct answer in Content. Mastery is at least 4 of 5 correct on the first attempt. Moving the temperature and drawing samples in free exploration is not evidence. **Misconceptions:** (1) A language model always gives the same answer to the same words (challenge 1 and free exploration). (2) A higher temperature makes the model more accurate or more "creative" without cost (challenges 2 and 5). (3) If the most likely word is correct, the model will never say the wrong one (challenge 3). (4) Temperature changes what the model knows, rather than how it chooses (challenge 4). **Instructional Rationale:** Understand-level inference needs the learner to predict an effect from the rule and then see whether the prediction holds. Committing to an answer before the sampled results appear forces that inference, and drawing 20 samples turns a probability into a visible count. **Content:** Four prompts, each with five candidate next words and their probabilities at temperature 1.0 (illustrative): | Prompt | Word 1 | Word 2 | Word 3 | Word 4 | Word 5 | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | 1. "Know ___" | thyself 60% | yourself 20% | the 10% | your 6% | nothing 4% | | 2. "Nothing in ___" | excess 55% | the 15% | particular 12% | life 10% | common 8% | | 3. "On Sundays the Grand Bazaar is ___" | closed 45% | open 30% | busy 15% | quiet 6% | crowded 4% | | 4. "The oracle at Delphi was ___" | consulted 30% | famous 25% | a 20% | closed 15% | silent 10% | Probabilities after applying the temperature rule, in percent, rounded to one decimal (for checking the sim): | Prompt | Temperature 0.5 | Temperature 2.0 | |---|---|---| | 1 | 86.7 / 9.6 / 2.4 / 0.9 / 0.4 | 39.1 / 22.6 / 15.9 / 12.4 / 10.1 | | 2 | 85.0 / 6.3 / 4.0 / 2.8 / 1.8 | 35.8 / 18.7 / 16.7 / 15.2 / 13.6 | | 3 | 63.2 / 28.1 / 7.0 / 1.1 / 0.5 | 32.7 / 26.7 / 18.9 / 11.9 / 9.8 | | 4 | 40.0 / 27.8 / 17.8 / 10.0 / 4.4 | 24.9 / 22.7 / 20.3 / 17.6 / 14.4 | A fact note shown with prompt 3: "The Grand Bazaar is usually closed on Sundays (Chapter 2). The model's probabilities describe what is often written, not what is true." Five challenge questions, in this order: | # | Prompt and setting | Question | Choices | Correct answer | Why (shown as feedback) | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | 1 | Prompt 1, temperature 0 | In 20 tries, which word will the model choose? | thyself every time; mostly thyself, sometimes yourself; a different word each time | thyself every time | At temperature 0 the model always takes the most likely word, so the same words always get the same answer. | | 2 | Prompt 1, temperature raised from 1.0 to 2.0 | What happens to the probability of "nothing"? | It goes up; it goes down; it stays at 4% | It goes up | A higher temperature flattens the probabilities, so the least likely word rises from 4.0% to 10.1%. | | 3 | Prompt 3, temperature 1.0 | About how many of 20 sampled answers will say "open"? | about 0; about 6; about 15 | about 6 | At temperature 1 each word is chosen in proportion to its probability: 30% of 20 is 6, even though "open" is usually false. | | 4 | Prompt 1, temperature lowered from 1.0 to 0.5 | What is the probability of "thyself" now? | about 30%; about 60%; about 87% | about 87% | A lower temperature sharpens the probabilities toward the favorite: 60% becomes 86.7%. The model's knowledge is unchanged; only its way of choosing changed. | | 5 | Prompt 4 | At which temperature are the five words closest to equally likely? | 0; 0.5; 2.0 | 2.0 | The highest temperature flattens the most: at 2.0 the five range only from 24.9% to 14.4%. | **Provenance:** All probabilities are illustrative, invented to show the rule; the sim labels them "Illustrative probabilities, not from a real model." The temperature rule is the standard softmax-temperature rescaling described in the chapter section "Next-Word Prediction." The Grand Bazaar fact is from Chapter 2, "Artificial Intelligence." **Rules:** - Temperature T: minimum 0.0, maximum 2.0, step 0.1, default 1.0, no unit. - For T > 0: adjusted probability of word i = p_i^(1/T) divided by the sum over all five words of p_j^(1/T). Display to one decimal place. - For T = 0: the most likely word has probability 100% and the others 0%. (No prompt has a tie for first place.) - Draw 20: draws 20 independent samples from the adjusted probabilities and shows how many times each word was chosen. Counts always total 20. Samples are random each time; a new draw replaces the previous counts. - Changing the prompt or the temperature clears the previous counts. - Challenge mode: the prompt and temperature are set by the challenge and locked until the learner has committed an answer and pressed Reveal; Reveal then shows the adjusted probabilities and a fresh draw of 20. **Learner Activity:** 1. The learner reads challenge 1 and chooses an answer. 2. The learner presses Reveal. The adjusted probabilities and a draw of 20 appear, followed by the feedback. 3. The learner continues through challenges 2 to 5. 4. After challenge 5, free exploration unlocks: the learner chooses any prompt, moves the temperature, and draws samples as often as they like. 5. In free exploration, the learner should notice that at temperature 1.0, prompt 3 produces "open" in some draws, and that at temperature 0 it never does. **Feedback:** Five challenges, fixed order, one scored attempt each. Correct: "Correct:" followed by the Why text. Incorrect: "Not quite. The answer is [correct answer]:" followed by the Why text. A running count "Correct on first attempt: n of 5" is shown. After challenge 5: if the score is at least 4, "You can predict what temperature does: it changes how the model chooses, not what it knows."; otherwise, "Try challenges 2 and 4 again in free exploration: watch the bars as you move the temperature." **Starting State:** Challenge 1 is shown: prompt 1, temperature locked at 0, the five candidate words with no bars yet, and the question "In 20 tries, which word will the model choose?" **Chapter Anchors:** The chapter's worked example uses prompt 1 with thyself 60, yourself 20, the 10, your 6, nothing 4 percent, and gives 86.7 / 60.0 / 39.1 percent for "thyself" and 0.4 / 4.0 / 10.1 percent for "nothing" at temperatures 0.5, 1.0 and 2.0. It states that about 3 answers in 10 to prompt 3 will say "open" at temperature 1, with closed 45 and open 30 percent. Temperature 0 always takes the most likely word.
